correctness.rationale: Repeated independent trials of a fixed reset word give a geometric tail, ensuring finite moments and uniqueness of the transient-chain equations. Before reaching the boundary j=n−1, a rotation advances the pair and a merge leaves it unchanged; this produces a drop of 2 in both mean and variance per advancement. At the boundary reached from {0,d}, let L=n−1−d; the successors are {0,L+1} and {0,L}, with the latter absorbed for L=0. For the mean the boundary equation is F_d=2L+1+(F_(L+1)+F_L)/2. For variance the law of total variance gives G_d=2L+(G_(L+1)+G_L)/2+(F_(L+1)−F_L)²/4. Direct symbolic substitution gives zero polynomial residuals, and F_0=G_0=0. The strictly concave quadratic F_d has vertex n(n−1)/(2n−1), whose closest integer is floor(n/2) for both parities; the term −2i makes i=0 unique. At this gap the mean and variance have leading terms n³ and 2n⁶/3, giving the stated coefficient of variation, not a distributional limit. An independently written exact-rational replay (`python3 reproductions/2.py --max-n 8`) matched all 83 pair states for n=3,…,8; the frozen verifier was inspected, not run. The recurrence identities, not the finite replay, establish the claim for every n.
